description: The divergence-recovery test (PROP-714, 'a push rejected by a non-fast-forward divergence is recovered') triggers the rejection by having an OUTSIDE clone push a commit directly onto the exclusive per-instance branch `ledger-franklin` (test lines 422-429). But REQ-705's own text (behavioral-spec.md:217-220) calls exactly this scenario 'structurally impossible': 'no two instances ... ever write to the same branch'. The test therefore proves recoverFromDivergence()'s MECHANICS work once triggered, but never proves the mechanism is reachable in the real, single-writer-per-branch production topology this design otherwise guarantees. Per FIND-002 (this review), the realistic same-instance trigger for a lost-write scenario -- publishRepoDir being lost/recreated between a local commit and its eventual push -- produces a clean fast-forward, NOT a rejected push, so it is never caught by this test or by the code path it exercises. A reader of this suite would reasonably conclude divergence-safety is proven end-to-end for this feature's actual deployment; it is not.

corroborating.note: explicitly frames cross-writer collision on the same branch as structurally impossible -- the test's own trigger contradicts the design's stated invariant.
